text:
Clara: Heads-up — DeepLeaf onboarding reported recurring tail latency and token-cost spikes on long-context exports today. Renewal touchpoint in 10d. p95 jumped from ~2.1s to ~7.4s on 12k+ token runs. Can we propose a low-friction ops plan to present in the renewal sync? :worried:
Jin: Oof. Do we have model + route + quant state?
Clara: They're on hosted `gptx-3-8b`, default routing, no quant. Load pattern: nightly bulk exports + occasional long interactive sessions.
Sienna: Two low-risk levers that synergize: (1) soft-int8 profile (weights int8, keep critical ops fp16) to reduce runtime without large quality drift; (2) token-split routing so heavy exports hit a dedicated compact pool. Both can be canaried independently.
Rahul: Agree. Add prefix caching for repeated headers and micro-batching for export jobs to reduce per-request overhead. That often buys a lot on export-heavy customers.
Clara: We need an immediate plan we can run this week. Proposed quick plan:
  1) Eval: 15 representative DeepLeaf prompts (mix long exports + edge cases) vs soft-int8. Run automated checks + 5 manual spot-checks. (owners: Jin + Sienna)
  2) Canary: route long-export requests (prompt_tokens >= 4096) to dedicated-compact-softint8 in us-west at 5% traffic for 3h. ops-bot to provision.
  3) Fallback: if cohort error-rate > 0.6% OR p95 > 9s -> immediate reroute to hosted-default and abort canary.
  4) If stable: escalate 5% -> 35% (12h) -> 75% (24h) -> full, gated by quality + CS signoff. Capture user feedback after 6h and 24h.
Jin: Safety note on soft-int8: we've seen tiny punctuation drift on very contrived code-like prompts. Recommend running token-delta and hallucination checks on the eval.
Sienna: I'll prepare the route rule and the canary script. Pseudocode for route:
```
if prompt_tokens >= 4096 and customer_tag == 'deepleaf':
  route -> dedicated-compact-softint8-usw1
else:
  route -> hosted-lowlatency
```
Will include header guard so only their traffic is affected.
Rahul: Eval command I'll run:
```
python3 run_eval.py --base=gptx-3-8b --alt=gptx-3-8b-soft-int8 --prompts=deepleaf_eval.json --metrics=perplexity,token_delta,hallucination
```
I'll post artifacts link and quick summary in ~60m.
Clara: Also add an enablement note: suggest client-side micro-batching for exports (2-3 docs/request) and a config to prime prefix cache for repeated report headers. Low lift on their SDK. We'll include suggested snippet in the CS packet.
ops-bot: Provisioning request received (job: prov-2987). ETA dedicated pool ~6m. Canary template: 5% for 3h.
Jin: One more ask — include a fallback routing policy: on 5xx or latency > 12s for 1 minute -> fallback to hosted-default. Avoid cascading failures.
Sienna: Will add that. Also will log and store 50 sampled responses to cs-audit/deepleaf/ for the renewal deck.
ops-bot: Dedicated pool ready. Will deploy route rule and start canary at 04:18 UTC.
Rahul: Eval results (50m): perplexity delta +1.1%, token_delta within threshold, manual spot-check 0/5 major diffs. Artifacts: https://console.redwood/cs/artifacts/deepleaf/2987654321
ops-bot: Canary started. 5% long-export traffic -> dedicated-compact-softint8-usw1. Health checks every 5m.
Jin: Early telemetry (first 40m): canary cohort p95 down to ~2.0s vs baseline 7.4s. No error-rate or quality alerts so far.
Clara: I'll message the CSM and schedule a short check-in in 6h to capture qualitative feedback for the renewal. If 24h stable, recommend staged rollout. Thanks team :raised_hands:
Sienna: I'll leave fallback active and set escalation to 35% in 3h if no regressions.
Rahul: I'll archive eval logs + regression checklist into the customer's CS folder and attach to the renewal note.
Clara: Closing loop: owners recap — Jin (quality signoff + watch), Sienna (routing + fallback + artifact capture), Rahul (eval + customer folder), ops-bot (canary + monitor). Will follow up after 24h.
